name: Rockweed: knotted wrack in shelter, bladder wrack where exposed
plain: Rockweed covers rock between the tides; knotted wrack (Ascophyllum) on sheltered shores, bladder wrack (Fucus) and barnacles where the waves hit.
confidence: medium: curves from World's levels/downeast/coast_rules.json (21 Oct), checked against the Bar Harbor shore and cited above; Matt's field corrections still to come

sources.cite: Stephenson, T.A. & Stephenson, A. (1949) The universal features of zonation between tide-marks on rocky coasts. J. Ecol. 37: 289-305.
sources.note: the fucoid belt in the mid-intertidal

sources.note: Ascophyllum dominates sheltered Gulf of Maine shores; Fucus and barnacles take over with exposure
